title: FDA clarifies policies for compounders as national GLP-1 supply begins to stabilize
journal: US Food and Drug Administration, Drug Safety and Availability, updates of 19 December 2024 to 28 April 2025
result: On 21 February 2025 FDA determined that the shortage of semaglutide injection products, in shortage since 2022 because of increased demand, was resolved after confirming with the manufacturer that availability and manufacturing capacity could meet present and projected national demand. FDA stated it would not act against state-licensed pharmacies or physicians compounding essentially copies of the approved product under section 503A until 22 April 2025, or against outsourcing facilities under section 503B until 22 May 2025; after a district court denied a preliminary injunction on 24 April 2025, the 503A period of enforcement discretion ended. The tirzepatide injection shortage was declared resolved on 19 December 2024.
